summary: Iteration 16 — File & media storage integration. 12/12 backend pytest cases pass. Focus areas E1 handed off (WebSocket delivery of attachments, cross-user attachment/upload-session abuse, admin delete, size caps, partner gallery E2E, legacy image regression) all pass end-to-end. Frontend UI on Messages page (attachment-btn, attachment-preview, attachment-remove) works at 1920px and 390px with no horizontal overflow and WS state 'Live'. Partner event form gallery works when adding photos ONE AT A TIME (upload -> item-0 appears -> upload again -> item-1 appears -> remove-0 works). One reproducible frontend bug found: selecting multiple photos in a SINGLE file picker leaves only the last photo (stale closure over `value` inside the sequential upload loop in GalleryUpload.jsx). Also cleaned up 24 leftover 'TEST hello ...' messages from a prior run in conversation 6a7b6792aaea7f778441926c (per E1's cleanup ask) and reset that conversation's last_message to a real value.

minor.issue: Sess.received is incremented BEFORE the update_one write of the chunk (line 2417 uses $inc after upsert). If a client retries the same index the size is double-counted and can trip the 'exceeded declared file size' guard on a legitimate retry. Consider $set:{received: sum(parts.data.size)} or dedupe by index.

The path query param is not URL-decoded/validated as belonging to the app namespace. In practice storage_path is only assigned via our code so injection risk is low, but a defensive `startswith(APP_NAME + '/uploads/')` check would be cheap.

ui_bugs.issue: Selecting multiple photos in a single file-picker keeps ONLY the last uploaded photo. The for-loop closes over the initial `value` prop, so each iteration re-computes `[...value, data.url]` from the same stale array. Adding photos one at a time works because the component re-renders between picks. Fix: track a running local array (`let next = [...value]; ... next = [...next, data.url].slice(0, max); onChange(next);`) inside `pick`.

action_items: Fix GalleryUpload.jsx multi-select bug (see ui_bugs) so picking 2+ photos in one dialog adds all of them.
(Optional) Recompute `sess.received` from parts rather than $inc, so retried chunks don't inflate the counter.
(Optional) Defensive path prefix check in DELETE /api/uploads.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L2415-2417: upload_chunk_part uses upsert on (upload_id, index) — good for idempotency of storage — but then blindly $inc's sess.received by len(data). A retry of the same index therefore double-counts and can hit the (size + CHUNK_LIMIT_BYTES) guard on L2413. Compute received from db.upload_parts sum after each write, or only $inc when insert (upserted_id is not None).
server.py L2426: complete() reads up to 200 parts. MAX_FILE_BYTES=25MB / CHUNK_LIMIT_BYTES=3MB → max 9 parts, so 200 is safe, but this is a magic upper bound worth documenting.

server.py L2466 GET /api/files/{path}: no Cache-Control set. Static-served images benefit from short-term caching (Cache-Control: private, max-age=60) so the browser doesn't re-hit /api/files on every message re-render.
GalleryUpload.jsx L20-22: multi-file loop closure bug (see ui_bugs).

GalleryUpload.jsx L55: helper text claims 'up to 25MB each' but /uploads/file caps images at 5MB and only the chunked path allows 25MB — the label is misleading for image gallery photos (which are always PNG/JPG/WEBP). Prefer 'up to 5MB each' to match the enforcement in upload_any.

rca of the issue: GalleryUpload multi-select bug — in components/GalleryUpload.jsx the pick() handler iterates awaited uploadFile() calls, but each `onChange([...value, data.url])` reads `value` from the closure captured at render time. Because React state updates are asynchronous and the same closure is used for every iteration, iteration N still sees the initial `value`, so only the last iteration's onChange sticks. Repro: pick 2 photos in a single file dialog → gallery shows only the 2nd. Mitigation: track the running array locally: `let next = value.slice(); for (...) { next = [...next, data.url].slice(0, max); onChange(next); }`.
